summary: Encoded the owner-requested general logical rule for joint route settlement. Indexed route completion, existential failed premise and universal failure consequences make the coverage burden explicit. A Bool control rejects replacing universal failure coverage with a single sampled implication; the common-obligation theorem shows why cross-route composition cannot avoid a proposition required by every covered route. This is a logical template over opaque proposition families, not an instantiated Catholicism argument. Revelation recognizability remains shared and open. No philosophical consequence of a route failure or floor candidate is established by the template.
blocker: A concrete joint settlement still needs consequences covering every failure mode of both chosen routes and an incompatibility established from settled premises under one shared semantic profile. The same open premise shared by all routes cannot be evaded by their disjunction.
